description: A large-scale training data collection for long video understanding, centered on LongVid — a long video instruction-tuning dataset comprising 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 QA pairs across five task types (video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting), containing 300,000 hours of videos and 2 billion words of textual annotations.
name: VideoChat-Flash Training Data (LongVid)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: QA pairs are constructed automatically from video captions, event labels, and timestamps of short video segments. Five task types are generated: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting. For event relation recognition, models choose the correct order of event sequences. For temporal grounding, short video captions with timestamps serve as ground truth with randomly selected false options.
rai:dataCollection: LongVid is curated from four open-source video datasets: Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData. Dense event labels are generated for each long video using existing high-quality short video captions (Panda-70M for HD-VILA, CosMo for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D, and original captions from MiraData). Consecutive segments are filtered and regrouped into long video sequences, then QA pairs are constructed based on captions, event labels, and timestamps.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data includes videos from Ego4D (egocentric videos), HowTo100M (how-to instructional videos), HD-VILA (in-the-wild videos), and MiraData (movie segments). Captions come from Panda-70M, CosMo/HowToInterlink7M, Ego4D-HCap, and MiraData's original captions. Event annotations come from HT-Step (for HowTo100M) and Ego4D-HCap (for Ego4D).
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Duration-based sampling is applied: for short videos (D < Tmin), dense sampling is used; for long videos (D > Tmax), sparse sampling is used. In Stage 3, the number of sampled video frames ranges from 64 to 512. Short and long video data are mixed to ensure the model retains fine-grained understanding while expanding comprehension of long videos.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Consecutive video segments are filtered and regrouped into long video sequences (over 60 seconds). Event labels are extracted from captions using an LLM (Qwen-72b) for datasets without high-quality event-level annotations. For datasets with existing event annotations (HT-Step for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D), those are used directly. Captions in Stage 2 are refined using AI models for richer descriptions.
rai:dataUseCases: Training multimodal large language models for long video understanding, including tasks such as video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting. Supports short-to-long learning strategies for video MLLMs.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen-72b LLM (for extracting event and background labels from captions in MiraData and HD-VILA); VideoChat2 (for recaptioning WebVid2M videos); Gemini (for recaptioning WebVid and Kinetics videos); LLava-NeXT-34B (for recaptioning image description data from COCO118K, BLIP558K, CC3M); GPT-4o (for annotating short video data including ShareGPT4o, VideoChatGPT-Plus).

evidence.name: we introduce a large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset named LongVid. It comprises 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering (QA) pairs across five different task types, supporting models to handle diverse long video scenarios.

evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: we filter the consecutive segments that can be regroup into a long video sequence, then we construct a sequence of event labels with their corresponding timestamps for every long video based on their captions. evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Finally, we construct several types of long video QA pairs based on the video captions, event labels, and the timestamps of short video segments. They are categorized into five tasks: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.
